heading: INT. ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE APARTMENT, LISBON - EVENING

units.text: INT. ROOFTOP GREENHOUSE APARTMENT, LISBON - EVENING
A small glass room on a tiled roof.
Geraniums in chipped pots.
Behind the glass the city falls away in terraces of orange light and the river beyond is the colour of tin.
CATARINA VIEIRA, thirty-five, in a linen shirt, stands at a wooden table with her sleeves rolled.
She waters a row of seedlings from a copper can.
She hums as she works, tunelessly, content.
On the table, a battered answering machine blinks red.
She does not look at it.
She waters.
She hums.
She leans to pinch a dead leaf from a geranium.
She straightens.
Her eyes finally go to the machine.
She presses a finger to the button.
You've reached Catarina. If you're Tomás, I'm still angry. If you're not Tomás, leave a message.
units.name: MACHINE

units.text: A beep.
Her hand goes still on the can.
It's me. I'm at the airport. I just wanted to say I'm sorry, and I'm coming back, and, and I changed the message so you'd have it.
units.name: CATARINA

units.text: She sets the can down.
She presses the button again.
She listens again.
Her lips move along with the words.
Then she lowers herself into the chair beside the table.
She turns the machine until its small red eye faces the window, toward the river, and she smiles.
She picks up the can.
She waters the seedlings.
She hums.
